title: Honey Lemon Chicken
leftover_note: Reheats in the pan; turn to coat in the sauce.
instructions: Slice each chicken breast horizontally to form 4 steaks in total. Optional (for more even cooking): pound to even thickness about 1 cm / 2/5" thick.
Sprinkle each side generously with salt and pepper.
Place the flour in a shallow dish. Coat the chicken in the flour, shaking off excess.
Mix 1 tsp of the flour (reserved from step 3) with the water. Set aside.

Place the oil and olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until hot. Add the chicken and cook for 2 minutes or until golden brown. Turn and cook the other side until golden brown, then transfer to a plate to rest.
Add the garlic to the skillet and stir for 20 seconds or until golden. Add the chicken broth and bring to a simmer, scraping the brown bits from the bottom of the pan into the liquid.
Add the honey, lemon juice, soy sauce, and flour/water mixture to the skillet. Mix and bring to a simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until thickened into a syrup. Add salt and pepper to taste.
To serve, pour the sauce over the chicken and garnish with parsley and lemon slices if using. Alternatively, return the chicken to the pan for 30 seconds (to reheat), turning to coat in the sauce.

tips.title: Extra juicy chicken
tips.text: Bringing the chicken to room temperature really helps it cook very fast, keeping it extra juicy.

tips.title: Veggie bonus
tips.text: Blanch asparagus or other fairly flat vegetables in the sauce while it simmers — add 1/4 cup of water and cook the veggies until crisp-tender.

tips.title: Freezing
tips.text: Don't freeze the chicken in the sauce (it goes soggy when stored). Freeze the sauce separately from the cooked chicken.

Printed times (5 min prep, 7 min cook, serves 4) are for the original 1-lb recipe and were adjusted up for the doubled version.
